headline: Uniqueness of the cycle is proved for large gain (k >= 1000 max(1, mu^3)) and near each Hopf point; it is NOT proved for all oscillatory parameters.

status_vocabulary.proved: complete proof in the paper; imported results are named
status_vocabulary.proved_conditional: complete proof given a named hypothesis taken from the literature
status_vocabulary.floating_point_evidence: supported by ordinary floating-point computation only
status_vocabulary.refuted_floating_point: contradicted by floating-point computation at stated parameters

claims.label: thm:largegain
claims.statement: For 0 < mu <= 1 and k >= 1000 every cycle satisfies T >= 0.1833 lambda/mu, has slope p >= 0.819 lambda at the up-crossing of U = 0, has a crest interval of explicit short duration, and satisfies <eta> <= 0.83 mu < mu; it is hyperbolic and attracting.

claims.label: cor:lgunique
claims.statement: For 0 < mu <= 1 and k >= 1000 there is exactly one cycle and it attracts every orbit of the positive domain off the one-dimensional stable manifold of the equilibrium.

claims.label: cor:lgreciprocal
claims.statement: For mu >= 1 and k >= 1000 mu^3 the same conclusions hold. Only cycles and Floquet multipliers are transported by the reciprocal-rate correspondence; the positive domains do not correspond.

claims.label: thm:mainlarge
claims.statement: In original rates: if r0 >= 1000 max(a0,b0)^2 / min(a0,b0) the system has exactly one positive cycle; it is hyperbolic, attracting, and attracts every positive solution off the stable manifold of the equilibrium.

claims.label: thm:attractor
claims.statement: (A1)-(A5), all mu,k > 0: the log-bounded entire orbits form a compact connected global attractor; positive adjoint ratios exist uniquely along each; strict supporting planes hold between any two of its points; the attractor is the graph of the restriction of a convex function over its planar projection, C^1 in the interior with gradient (zeta, -eta); the reduced planar field has divergence eta - mu. (A6)-(A8), k > k_H: E is a source in the attractor; the projection is the closed Jordan domain bounded by the outermost projected cycle; planar multipliers equal m_t; innermost and outermost cycles have lambda_c <= 0.

claims.label: thm:twoorbit
claims.statement: Strict supporting-plane comparison for any two distinct log-bounded entire solutions.

claims.label: cor:criterion
claims.statement: Parameter-wise criterion: if every cycle at (mu,k) has lambda_c < 0, the cycle is unique, hyperbolic, attracting, and is the omega-limit set of every positive orbit off the stable manifold of E; if there are two cycles, one has lambda_c >= 0.

claims.label: prop:crestaxis
claims.statement: Return map on the crest half-axis of the attractor: derivative formula through the one-turn integral of eta - mu; conditional uniqueness criteria. The two monotonicity hypotheses of its last part are NOT proved and fail in floating point at extreme rate ratios.

claims.label: thm:gauges
claims.statement: On every cycle Sigma = p^2 - U p' > 0 and Xi = p'^2 - p p'' > 0: the (U,p) projection is strictly star-shaped about the origin and strictly convex; lambda_c = -<pK/Sigma> = -<pW/Xi>; an explicit state function eta_0 has mean mu and eta - eta_0 = -pK/Sigma.

claims.label: prop:kappa
claims.statement: kappa = K/Sigma solves a scalar Riccati equation with explicit coefficients; lambda_c T = -integral of (kappa_up - kappa_down) dU.

claims.label: prop:polar
claims.statement: Polar form of the projected flow and of the weak exponent.

claims.label: prop:nestedradii
claims.statement: For two nested cycles the radial ratio is monotone on each half-plane.

claims.label: prop:monotoneintegrals
claims.statement: <(alpha p + beta p')(alpha eta + beta zeta)> < 0 for (alpha,beta) != 0.

claims.label: prop:holder
claims.statement: <x^(1/3)>^3 < gamma(gamma-1)(gamma-mu) < k on every cycle.

claims.label: prop:lvchain
claims.statement: Cyclic Lotka-Volterra form; second-order equation for eta; an explicit pair solving the first Riccati equation with mean mu.

claims.label: prop:strongidentity
claims.statement: Exact pairing identity for lambda_c with the strong-stable solution; comparison (supersolution) bound.

claims.label: prop:gaussmap
claims.statement: The map from cycle points to (eta, zeta) is injective.

claims.label: lem:strongstable
claims.statement: Strong-stable Floquet vector e_s = (a,-b,-c) with a,b,c > 0 and the equations of its ratios; lambda_c < 0 iff the mean of b/a is below A.

claims.label: thm:twelve
claims.statement: Each component of the weak adjoint has exactly two simple zeros per period, in a fixed order with the six extrema.

claims.label: thm:dualsupport
claims.statement: The plane spanned by the tangent and the strong-stable vector strictly supports the cycle, the equilibrium and nested inner cycles.

claims.label: prop:crestmonotone
claims.statement: The crest return map exists, is C^1 and has an entrywise positive derivative on the region {p = 0, k e^U >= y > k}.

claims.label: prop:rankone
claims.statement: Rank-one window identity: every periodic test function gives the same single unknown sign.

claims.label: prop:multipliers
claims.statement: Positive transverse multipliers m_s < m_t with exact exponents; lambda_c = <eta> - mu.

claims.label: prop:factor
claims.statement: Tangent orthogonality and factorisation of the scalar variational operator.

claims.label: thm:support
claims.statement: Strict supporting planes with a cycle or the equilibrium as base.

claims.label: cor:cones
claims.statement: K > 0, Lambda_E > 0 and exclusion of both closed cones.

claims.label: thm:geometry
claims.statement: Injective regular clockwise planar projection; one crest and one trough; nested cycles.

claims.label: thm:six
claims.statement: Six nondegenerate extrema in the fixed order X_min, Z_min, Y_min, X_max, Z_max, Y_max.

claims.label: prop:crestmap
claims.statement: Entrywise positive crest-return derivative with determinant e^{-AT} < e^{-4 pi}; T > 2 pi / sqrt(mu).

claims.label: thm:compact
claims.statement: Uniform compactness of cycle families on compact subsets of the oscillatory domain (state box, separation from E, bounded least periods).

claims.label: lem:collar
claims.statement: Global uniqueness in a non-explicit right-hand neighbourhood of each Hopf point.

claims.label: thm:neutral
claims.statement: The neutral parameter set is relatively closed; the cycle count is locally constant off it; non-uniqueness at a finite parameter requires a neutral cycle on the fixed-mu path from the collar.

claims.label: obs:cor:uniqueset
claims.statement: The set of parameters at which every cycle has lambda_c < 0 is open, its boundary lies in the neutral set, and it contains the Hopf collars and the large-gain region.

claims.label: lem:tauidentities
claims.statement: Exact identities on every cycle in frequency-one time.

claims.label: thm:kurtosis
claims.statement: For a strictly convex potential, <P^4> <= (9/5)<P^2>^2 on every level; the selection function is a bijection with derivative at least 4/5.

claims.label: thm:wedge
claims.statement: Small rate ratio, rho - 1 = r eps^2 with r in a compact interval: exactly one cycle in a fixed energy ball, hyperbolic attracting, with an asymptotic formula for log m_t. Local in phase space; mu_0 not explicit; NOT a global uniqueness statement.
imports: Eldering Theorem 3.2; explicit cutoff application in Lemma wed:lem:slowgraph

claims.label: thm:failed
claims.statement: The square-root radial contraction certificate fails near Hopf for 0 < mu < 1.

claims.label: prop:nodulac
claims.statement: Constraints on Dulac functions for the reduced flow: none regular at E; only one sign is possible.

claims.label: prop:nomonomial
claims.statement: No vector supersolution of monomial form in the chemical variables exists on any cycle above Hopf.

claims.label: lem:rigidity
claims.statement: Any certificate direction must agree with the true adjoint pair to first order at Hopf.

claims.label: neg:prop:signchange
claims.statement: Conditional: a single sign change of the one-turn integral of eta - mu along the crest half-axis implies uniqueness. The hypothesis is unproved.

not_proved.statement: Exactly one cycle at every parameter k > mu(1+mu) (the conjecture of Smith 2012).
not_proved.known: true for k >= 1000 max(1, mu^3) and in non-explicit Hopf collars

not_proved.note: equivalent, up to the degenerate case lambda_c = 0, to uniqueness at each parameter

not_proved.statement: The one-turn mean of eta - mu is strictly decreasing in crest amplitude on the attractor.
not_proved.note: would imply uniqueness; held at every parameter tested

not_proved.statement: No second cycle and no cycle with lambda_c >= 0 exists in the open region.
Global uniqueness in the small-rate-ratio wedge.
